scene_summary: Raised embroidery on coral-orange woven cloth: a large smiling green long-necked turtle with a cream-spotted brown shell faces a separate blue grand piano. Three cream musical symbols bridge the open field. Lavender stitch clusters and broken green perimeter ribs provide subordinate accents. The creature is the single planned source-bearing anchor.
usable_surfaces: Raised green head and curved neck embroidery
Cream-outlined brown shell with cream stitched spots

detected_objects.label: Smiling green long-necked turtle with cream-spotted brown shell
detected_objects.visual_evidence: The left-hand figure has a rounded green head with two dark eyes and a curved smile, a long bending green neck, a broad brown shell outlined in cream yarn, multiple cream shell spots, and short green feet beneath the shell. Dense directional stitches and small shadows visibly distinguish the raised figure from the orange woven ground. Its head faces the separate piano; no appendage touches the keyboard.

effect_material.observation: Raised green, brown and cream yarn forms the creature above an orange woven ground. Directional stitches, cream contour cords and small edge shadows visibly establish shallow textile relief and a textured surface; no reflective finish, open fracture or vibrating component is visible.

effect_editorial.source_observation: The pixels show a physical embroidered patch with an orange field and lime-green stitched border. A smiling green cartoon turtle plays a blue grand piano beside a musical note, framed by stitched lettering reading “TRY MUSIC / YOU MIGHT LIKE IT.” Visible thread texture establishes the textile artwork itself; verification does not rely on the saved-note attribution or caption. No software interface, tool demonstration, sponsored event advertisement, or administrative CTA is visible.

effect_editorial.brief_quote: Directional thread and pale contours retain handmade character.
effect_editorial.why_behavior: The inspected source establishes embroidery, and the plate preserves visibly raised thread. That supports shallow relief technically, but moving the creature as a separate depth layer would exaggerate the construction into a cutout rather than clarify its stitches.
effect_editorial.why_input: Neither pointer movement nor device tilt has a source-specific role here. A stationary source-opening interaction is sufficient and avoids making ordinary navigation move the embroidered figure.
effect_editorial.why_not_none: The existing thread directions and edge shadows already reveal the relief. Leaving the plate undisturbed preserves the handmade surface and the quiet separation between creature and piano.

effect_editorial.brief_quote: Sparse cream notes bridge the gap; raised lid, pale keys and slender legs remain distinct.
effect_editorial.why_behavior: The source inspection describes a musical scene, but this mapped mark is an embroidered creature rather than a playable instrument. Touch-generated sound would assign an invented sonic behavior to the turtle without revealing anything about the inspected textile.
effect_editorial.why_input: A tap on the creature belongs to source discovery. Using that same gesture to synthesize sound would add an unrelated action; visible yarn texture alone does not justify a touch effect.
effect_editorial.why_not_none: Silence leaves the musical association legible through the notes, facing direction and separate piano. Added synthesized notes would supply content not established by the source inspection.

complexity_assessment.rationale: Two dominant embroidered figures occupy an open orange field. Small notes, lavender stitches and broken border ribs remain subordinate. The plate is illustrative rather than strongly expressionist, but its sparse arrangement is not cluttered. Only the planned creature is mapped; supporting motifs receive no additional source bindings.

effects_editorial_context.brief: Landscape embroidery: a large smiling green long-necked creature with cream-spotted taupe shell faces a smaller blue grand piano across broad coral-orange weave. Sparse cream notes bridge the gap; raised lid, pale keys and slender legs remain distinct. One offset lavender stitch cluster replaces lettering; broken green perimeter ribs frame the field. Directional thread and pale contours retain handmade character.
effects_editorial_context.aesthetic_thesis: An imagined cartoon rehearsal room where a blue grand piano and a patient turtle turn musical hesitation into a welcoming visual joke.
